Oral Judgment

Aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.1448/2021 dated 04.02.2023 by the Addl. Small Causes and Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Mysuru, whereby the tribunal had fixed the liability on the owner of the vehicle, both the insurance company and the claimant are before this court.
The Claimant's appeal is MFA No.3538/2023 and the insurance Company's appeal is MFA No.3620/2023.
NC: 2025:KHC:36353 HC-KAR 2.

The Tribunal had granted compensation of an amount of Rs.4,59,700/- as per the table given below:

Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid driving license as on the date of the accident and the tribunal has failed to observe the charge sheet, which clearly shows that the driver did not possess valid and effective DL.
Hence, the principle of pay and recover will apply and the Tribunal had failed to consider the same.
It is submitted that when it comes to the compensation, the amounts that are granted by the Tribunal on all the counts are on the higher side.
NC: 2025:KHC:36353 HC-KAR 4.
Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that the Tribunal had failed to grant reasonable compensation on all the counts.
It is submitted that the Tribunal had failed to grant the reasonable amount under the head of loss of earning during the laid up period.
Considering the injuries, even for the loss of amenities the amount that is awarded is a meager amount.

When the doctor had opined that the disability is assessed at 25% to the limb, the tribunal had taken 10%
functional disability and hence, the compensation needs to be enhanced.
5.
Having heard the learned counsels on either sides, perused the material on record.

Coming to the contention of the insurance company with regard to applying the principle of pay and recover,
considering the charge sheet which clearly shows that the driver of the offending vehicle is not having a valid driving license and in the light of the law laid down in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Swaran Singh & others1, the principle of pay and recovery will apply.

Rs.1,25,500/- and Rs.2,59,200/- respectively and no interference is called for.
